hypothesis: Integrating an asymmetric prediction head with stop-gradient prediction targets into Decoupled Contrastive Learning (DCL) prevents gradient symmetry and feature shortcutting during pretraining. By forcing a bottleneck predictor MLP to predict stationary target projections across views while decoupling positive alignment from the negative loss denominator, the anti-aliased backbone learns higher-level, linear-evaluable representations.
rationale: In iter 12, DCL on anti-aliased ResNet-26 achieved 0.6144 accuracy. Empirical findings from MoCo v3 and BYOL demonstrate that symmetric contrastive loss can allow networks to exploit low-level image shortcuts between identical projection heads. Introducing a 2-layer bottleneck Predictor MLP (1024 -> 512 -> 1024) paired with stop-gradient target projections breaks gradient symmetry, forcing the 1.5x wider anti-aliased ResNet-26 backbone to encode semantic invariants rather than spatial shortcuts.
expected_effect: Improve top-1 validation accuracy beyond 0.6144 by enhancing feature representation quality through asymmetric contrastive target prediction.
change_summary:
1. Modified BarlowTwinsModel to split the 2048-d output into a 1024-d prediction vector (computed via a 2-layer bottleneck Predictor MLP: Linear(1024, 512) -> BN -> ReLU -> Linear(512, 1024)) and a 1024-d target projection vector (768 -> 2048 -> 2048 -> 1024).
2. Refactored BarlowTwinsLoss to implement Predictor-DCL: computes asymmetric contrastive loss between prediction p1 (or p2) and detached target projections t2.detach() (and t1.detach()), masking self-target entries in logsumexp calculations.
3. Retained anti-aliased ResNet-26 backbone (1.5x width, 768-dim features) and detail-preserving CIFAR-100 augmentations.
